title: Practice 4: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: After an awkward pause, Bill took her by the hand and dragged her upstairs.
exercises.why: **потащил** is the past tense (masculine) of **потащить** (to start pulling) — the perfective of **тащить**, «set out». past: он потащи́л · она потащи́ла · оно потащи́ло · они потащи́ли. — Wiktionary, «потащить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **таскал** is a form of **таскать** (to carry, to lug, to drag); **тащил** is a form of **тащить** (to pull, to drag, to haul).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.ru: После неловкой паузы Билл взял ее за руку и ___ наверх.
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Том ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)) на поправку.
exercises.why: **пойдёт** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». future: я пойду́ · ты пойдёшь · он пойдёт · мы пойдём · вы пойдёте · они пойду́т. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Я ___ (поехать — to set off (by vehicle)) в воскресенье.
exercises.why: **поеду** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **поехать** (to go (in a conveyance or on horseback)) — the perfective of **ехать**, «set out». future: я пое́ду · ты пое́дешь · он пое́дет · мы пое́дем · вы пое́дете · они пое́дут. — Wiktionary, «поехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The future perfective (поеду, поедешь) belongs to the 1st -е- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Мне надо ___ (сбегать — to run there and back) по делам.
exercises.why: **сбегать** (the infinitive) ((colloquial) to run (to a place) and get back, to run (for), to go and get) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. — Wiktionary, «сбегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Сколько астронавтов ___ (полететь — to fly off) на Луну?
exercises.why: **полетело** is the past tense (neuter) of **полететь** (to fly, to be flying) — the perfective of **лететь**, «set out». past: он полете́л · она полете́ла · оно полете́ло · они полете́ли. — Wiktionary, «полететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The perfective verb полететь (like пойти and поехать) denotes single action with the emphasis on the completed start. The past perfective (полетел, -ла, -ло, -ли) is formed in a regular way. The future perfective (полечу, полетишь) belongs to the 2nd (-и-) type of conjugation. The consonant "т" changes into "ч" in the first person singular only.» — DLI, Lesson 55.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «лететь — летать: perfective полететь · «for a while» полетать · «round trip» слетать.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Полковник полетел в Вашингтон.» (The Colonel flew to Washington. (single action; completed start)) — DLI, Lesson 55. «Завтра я полечу на фронт.» (Tomorrow I'll fly to the front. (single action)) — DLI, Lesson 55.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Я ___ (повести — to lead off, take along) себя агрессивно.
exercises.why: **повела** is the past tense (feminine) of **повести** (to lead, to conduct, to direct, to drive) — the perfective of **вести**, «set out». past: он повёл · она повела́ · оно повело́ · они повели́. — Wiktionary, «повести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **повести**: to lead, to conduct, to direct, to drive.  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «This verb also follows the pattern of "going verbs". Note the following meanings: 1. to lead, to take: Я веду моего сына в школу. Я каждый день вожу его в школу. 2. to drive: Кто ведёт эту машину? Он не умеет водить машину. 3. to conduct: Противник ведёт огонь. 4. to behave oneself: Этот мальчик плохо ведёт себя. Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Девушка ___ (походить — to walk about for a while) на мать.
exercises.why: **походила** is the past tense (feminine) of **походить** (to look like, to resemble [with на (na, + accusative) ‘to someone/something’]) — the perfective of **ходить** meaning «for a while». past: он походи́л · она походи́ла · оно походи́ло · они походи́ли. — Wiktionary, «походить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «a) Prefix "по-" denoting a perfective action of limited duration (an action "for a while"). The prefix "по-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: походить, поездить, полетать. These verbs denote a single completed action of limited duration, similar to the verb "погулять".» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Он походил по комнате и сел за стол.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Она ___ (поездить — to ride about for a while) за границей.
exercises.why: **поездила** is the past tense (feminine) of **поездить** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the perfective of **ездить** meaning «for a while». past: он пое́здил · она пое́здила · оно пое́здило · они пое́здили. — Wiktionary, «поездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «a) Prefix "по-" denoting a perfective action of limited duration (an action "for a while"). The prefix "по-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: походить, поездить, полетать. These verbs denote a single completed action of limited duration, similar to the verb "погулять".» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «Note the preposition: after "going verbs" or the verb "to send" the preposition "за" + Instr. is used to indicate the idea of "going after" or "sending for" something or somebody: Он пошёл за газетой. — He went after the newspaper. Пошлите за доктором. — Send for the doctor.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
